answer: The voyage multiplier is published, charged in summit, and wharf lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 727 identities would post 2214 proofs and burn roughly 42 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
